newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY JUNE CPI ROSE ON SEASONALITIES - CEN BANK.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY JUNE CPI ROSE ON SEASONALITIES - CEN BANK.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary said on Friday that a 18.7 percent year-on-year consumer price rise in June was due to unpredictable seasonal factors.
The NBH earlier forecast a 17.4 to 17.8 year-on-year CPI rise for June.
"The June price index was not a reflection of an overall inflationary pressure but the result of a phenomenon of an unexpected size," the NBH said in a statement.

The Central Statistical Office (KSH) published June CPI figures earlier on Friday and detailed figures showed that while the overall month-on-month increase was 1.7 percent, food prices, which have a weight of 28.6 percent in the index, rose 4.0 percent from May.
The KSH added that the rise was due to the seasonality of fruit and vegetable prices.
The NBH said one single factor, a 150 percent rise of potato prices accounted for 0.9 percent of the monthly 1.7 percent rise in June.
"Without it, the CPI increase would have been 0.8 percent," the NBH said.
It added that while inflation is fundamentally influenced by macroeconomics, nominal wages and leading prices, there are also temporary or seasonal factors that also affect inflation.
Therefore, it would be useful if, at the same with the publication of the CPI figures, an index adjusted for seasonalities would also be published, the NBH said.
